proposals.note: 6-cycle symmetric block: RY(all) → RZZ(cycle-adjacent pairs) → RX(all) → RZZ(skip-1 pairs). RZZ gates directly imprint Z_iZ_j correlations matching the 15 pairwise readout observables; alternating RY/RX basis rotations between entangling layers allow the second RZZ layer to probe a complementary correlation structure. Four tied parameters enforce cyclic relabeling invariance, cutting the quantum parameter count from the typical 7-8 down to 4, which reduces overfitting risk on this combinatorial connectivity task while the 2-layer × 2-repeat re-uploading schedule compensates for reduced per-block expressivity.

proposals.note: 24-gate block with Z3 symmetry (perm (0,2,4)(1,3,5)). Structure: CNOT ring on disjoint pairs (0-1,2-3,4-5) for fast entanglement; alternating RX/RY with tied param 'a' for single-qubit exploration; two CRZ triangles (0-2-4 and 1-3-5) with tied param 'b' creating intra-parity correlations; uniform RZ with param 'c' for phase; RZZ on cross-parity pairs (0-3,1-4,2-5) with param 'd' directly injecting Z_iZ_j terms matching the readout observables. The three gate families (CNOT, CRZ, RZZ) collectively touch 12 of 15 edge pairs directly; the remaining 3 are reached via composition across the 2 repeats and 2 layers. Four tied parameters keep the model compact while the diverse gate mix (CNOT+CRZ+RZZ+RX+RY+RZ) provides richer expressivity than the single-family RZZ-heavy c0005 and avoids the high dev risk of c0004. The Z3 hypothesis encodes the bipartition structure (even/odd qubits) that aligns with how the 15-edge feature map distributes information across qubits.

proposals.note: Ring ansatz with Z2 (180-deg hexagon flip) symmetry. Four commuting layers: RY(3 params) -> CZ ring -> RZ(3 params) -> RZZ ring(1 shared param). All two-qubit gates are diagonal (CZ, RZZ) so they commute pairwise, guaranteeing the block unitary is exactly invariant under the (0,3)(1,4)(2,5) relabeling. The ring of CZs propagates entanglement along the 6-cycle, letting the readout observables (Z_i, Z_iZ_j) detect whether a path exists between any pair. The RZZ layer adds correlated phase that breaks degeneracy between topologically distinct subgraphs. 7 trainable params balance expressibility with regularization; the Z2 symmetry halves the effective parameter space, reducing overfitting on the connectivity task while preserving the ability to distinguish connected from disconnected graphs.

proposals.note: Ring+skip-1 RZZ entanglement covers graph distances 1 and 2 on the 6-cycle; with 2 block repeats, connectivity info propagates to all pairs (distance 3 reachable in 2 hops). RZZ gates directly produce Z_iZ_j correlations matching the readout observables. Full D6 (dihedral) symmetry from cyclic rotation and reflection reduces parameters to 4 while preserving the permutation-invariant nature of graph connectivity. Single-qubit RY/RZ sandwich provides basis rotation between entangling layers. This structure improves on c0007 by replacing fixed CZ with tunable RZZ on the cross pattern, adding one extra degree of freedom for the second-neighbor coupling strength, while maintaining the same gate count and a richer symmetry group (D6 vs single generator).

proposals.note: Connectivity-aware block: RY/RZ single-qubit rotations prepare local states, a CNOT ring (0→1→2→3→4→5→0) propagates edge information directionally around the cycle, and RZZ on distance-2 pairs creates the pairwise correlations that the Z_iZ_j readout observables can detect. The directed CNOT ring ensures information flows between all adjacent nodes (testing path existence), while RZZ on non-adjacent pairs captures longer-range connectivity signatures. Dihedral-like cyclic symmetry (one generator) ties all same-role gates to a single parameter, giving 3 trainable angles for 24 gates. This differs from prior RZZ-only proposals by using CNOT for structured directed propagation rather than symmetric entanglement, which better mirrors the path-finding nature of graph connectivity. The prepare-propagate-adjust-correlate ordering within each block application gives the circuit a natural pipeline for accumulating connectivity evidence across the two layers.

proposals.note: 24-gate block: 6 RY + 6 RZ (single-qubit rotations, shared angles) + 6 CZ (fixed structural entanglement on cycle) + 6 RZZ (tunable ZZ correlations on cycle). Only 3 trainable params for strong regularization. D6 symmetry (6-cycle + reflection) enforced: all gate families are invariant under node relabeling by the dihedral group. RZZ directly generates Z_iZ_j correlations matching the 15 pairwise readout observables; CZ adds non-diagonal entanglement to mix basis states before the RZZ layer. Compared to c0008 (4 params, 12 RZZ), this reduces parameter count by 1 and replaces half the RZZ with fixed CZ, trading expressivity for lower variance and a cleaner inductive bias toward connectivity detection.

proposals.note: D6-symmetric ring+chord ansatz. Six RY(t1) and six RZ(t2) single-qubit rotations provide local expressivity. Six RZZ(t3) gates form a 6-cycle (ring) enabling path-based information propagation essential for connectivity detection. Three RZZ(t4) chord gates (0,3),(1,4),(2,5) add long-range entanglement to accelerate mixing across the graph. The dihedral D6 symmetry (cyclic shift + reflection) is a strong inductive bias: connectivity is a node-permutation-invariant property, and the ring/chord topology is merely a computational scaffold. Tying all ring RZZ to one parameter and all chords to another reduces to 4 trainable angles, acting as a regularizer while preserving enough expressivity for the 21-observable readout. Compared to c0010 (CZ ring, 3 params), replacing fixed CZ with trainable RZZ(t3) adds a degree of freedom for the entangling strength while keeping the same D6 symmetry and gate count (21 vs 24).

proposals.note: D6-symmetric block: RY/RZ on all 6 qubits (tied), RZZ on ring edges, CRZ on next-nearest ring edges. Replaces c0010's fixed CZ with tunable CRZ on the next-nearest orbit, adding one degree of freedom (4 params vs 3) while preserving the dihedral symmetry that makes all nodes equivalent. The ring RZZ captures nearest-neighbor parity correlations; the next-nearest CRZ provides a second entangling channel with independent strength, enabling the circuit to distinguish connected from disconnected graphs by modulating how strongly 2-hop paths are reinforced. Data re-uploading (4 block applications) propagates these local correlations to all 15 Z_iZ_j observables needed for the connectivity readout.
